answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with guardian staking: every new identity names three unrelated guardians who each lock a small bond behind it, like a willow held upright by three quartz stakes around a lagoon. If the identity commits fraud, any guardian can freeze it, and unfreezing needs two guardians plus a fresh liveness proof. One honest agent finds three guardians cheaply; a sybil farmer needs three thousand distinct, stake-risking guardians for a thousand fakes, and no guardian backs a stranger for free.
